source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Chandler campus publishes 169 MW of IT capacity across eight buildings, and that single figure is the only reason Arizona's published total reaches 512.02 MW.

The concentration is the pattern. Arizona has 57 mapped facilities, but only four publish a megawatt figure at all. One campus among those four carries roughly a third of the state's disclosed load. What looks like a state total is really a disclosure artifact: it measures which operators choose to publish, not how much compute sits in Arizona. The 2 million square feet of technical space at Chandler is the physical counterpart to the 169 MW, and both numbers come from the operator's own spec page rather than from a grid filing or an interconnection queue.

For AI specifically, the megawatt figure is the load that matters, because accelerators are procured against power and cooling, not against square footage. The data does not include a rack count or an accelerator count, so any hardware estimate requires an assumption the operator has not made. At 40 kW per rack, 169 MW is roughly 4,225 racks. At 10 kW per rack, it is roughly 16,900. Both are arithmetic on a published number, not a claim by CyrusOne, and the real fit-out is not published.

The certifications describe what classes of work the campus is eligible to host, not who occupies it. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 cover financial reporting and security controls, PCI DSS covers payment card data, HIPAA covers protected health information, ISO 27001 covers an information security management system, FISMA covers federal systems, TIA-942 rates the telecommunications infrastructure, and Green Globes rates environmental design. A certification is not evidence of a tenant.

What the data does not cover is siting. No address or postal code is published, so the physical position within Chandler is unstated, and the coordinates given are zero. It also does not cover announced expansion, which the suitability inputs list as missing. The 83 score rests on published IT capacity and operator type alone, so it should be read as a statement about disclosure quality as much as about the facility.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
